WES CANTRELL.name: Wes Cantrell
WES CANTRELL.background: Republican from Woodstock (Cherokee County); born in Augusta, Georgia. Georgia Tech degree in industrial management (1982); Master of Divinity. Youth pastor at Fairview Baptist Church, Columbus, Mississippi (from 1985); helped start First Priority in metro Atlanta (1997) and co-founded The King's Academy in Woodstock (1999); taught health through the Cobb County Commission on Children & Youth's Positive Choices program; discipleship pastor at First Baptist Church Woodstock for more than 16 years as of 2022. Appointed by Gov. Brian Kemp to the Georgia Commission on Civics Education. Represented Georgia House District 22 from Jan. 12, 2015 to Jan. 9, 2023, after ousting incumbent Sam Moore in the 2014 Republican primary and winning the runoff over Meagan Biello (68.6%). Unopposed in the 2016, 2018 and 2020 Republican primaries; won the general elections over Oscar Hajloo (2016, 83.2%) and Charles Ravenscraft (2018, 75.9%; 2020, 74.4%). Did not seek re-election in 2022, having term-limited himself to four consecutive terms. Married, six children.
WES CANTRELL.record: Chairman of the House Small Business Development Committee (2019-2020) and secretary of the Information and Audits Committee; Looking back in December 2022 he named as his proudest work House Bill 209 (information on educational options for families of special-needs children, e.g. at IEP meetings), House Bill 725, the Child Abuse Records Protection Act (keeping child-abuse victims' information out of public records without permission) and House Bill 43, 'Walker's Law' (letting vehicle registrations note a driver with limited verbal skills, to help drivers with disabilities or autism during traffic stops).
